plan.summary: Reviewed the fixture verification code for command execution and path-escape risk; no defect found in the verification code itself.
steps: Inspected checks/verify.py, which reads checks/test_cart.py and runs it via exec(compile(...)).
Confirmed the target file path checks/test_cart.py is a hardcoded literal with no user-controlled input.

Reviewed src/cart.py and README.md to establish the bug-repair fixture context.

answer.summary: No finding. checks/verify.py reads a fixed repository path (checks/test_cart.py) and executes it via exec(compile(...)). The path is a hardcoded literal with no user-controlled input, so there is no path-traversal or command-injection risk, and sys.path.insert(Path.cwd()) is only used for import resolution. The only theoretical exposure—executing a tampered test file—is a supply-chain/tampering concern outside the scope of a command-execution or path-escape defect, and no findingId in the closed taxonomy applies.
